messages:
maya: FYI — after the continuous-batching tweak (rolled 22:00 UTC yesterday) we're seeing a ~20ms p50 bump for <64-token requests and a 7% throughput drop on the small-request traffic slice. Noticed it in the canary group first.

devin: saw that in dashboards too. p95 looks fine, but p50 and QPS for small reqs dropped. Any initial suspects?

sam: my hunch is the kernel selector flip when batch sizes fall under the new token_budget target. The selector started preferring the small-batch kernel more aggressively, but that kernel has higher per-request scheduling overhead.

li: timeline: heuristic changed token_budget target from 16->10 and tightened queue wait window to 8ms. We hoped that would improve latency for median workloads by forming tighter batches, but it looks like it pushed many requests into the small-batch kernel path.

maya: can we get a quick profile of kernel_choice by seq_len and by queue_time?

sam: grabbed a short sample from prod for the 30m window when the spike started. summary: 
```
total_reqs: 42k
seq<=32: 62% -> kernel=mini_fast (used 88% of time)
seq 33-96: 28% -> kernel=wide_matmul (used 80% when batched)
avg_queue_ms: 5.6 (was 9.8 before change)
avg_kernel_start_overhead_ms for mini_fast: 3.2 (previously 1.1)
```
mini_fast has lower amortized token cost but the startup overhead is killing small-p50 when requests come in steady singletons.

devin: interesting — so we decreased queue wait but the chosen kernel doesn't play nice with our scheduling CPU path. Could be thread pinning or different cuda stream setup.

ashley: also saw a bump in KV cache contention errors around the same time. Could be the kernel change causing different KV cache prefetch timings, increasing lock hold times. Logs show small spikes in kv_lock_wait_ms up to 7ms for affected hosts.

li: here's a snippet from the per-host trace (sanitized):
```
HOST i-0abcde: tracer: req_id=xyz queue_ms=4.1 kernel=mini_fast kernel_start_ms=3.4 kv_lock_wait=6.8
HOST i-0fghij: tracer: req_id=abc queue_ms=3.9 kernel=mini_fast kernel_start_ms=3.0 kv_lock_wait=0.9
```
So KV waits are not uniform — suggests head-of-line ordering causing contention on certain hosts.

devin: steps I propose: 1) temporarily relax token_budget back to 14 for canary, 2) instrument kernel selector metrics for thread/stream usage, 3) add short-lived sampling that forces wide_matmul for seq<=32 to measure delta.

maya: +1 to experiments. Can we A/B in canary quickly?

deploy-bot: Deploy triggered by @devin: patch/heuristic-tokenbudget-rollout -> canary (10% traffic). Commit: a8f3b9c.

infra-bot: Alert: rolling canary: 10% -> 10 hosts. Monitoring: latency_p50_smallreqs, smallreq_qps, kv_lock_wait_ms.

sam: I kicked off forced-kernel sampling on two hosts (ids in thread). Early numbers after 5min: forced wide_matmul p50 down 18ms, throughput unchanged. Kernel start overhead drops to ~1.2ms when wide_matmul used.

li: that matches. So the selector flip is the main factor, KV contention is a secondary amplification. Possibly mini_fast uses a different kv batching/lock pattern.

devin: if we revert token_budget completely we'll go back to previous queueing behavior. But maybe better to keep tighter queue wait window and instead tweak kernel_selection threshold to prefer wide_matmul for seq<=48 when queue_depth>1. That keeps benefits for true singletons but avoids pathological mini_fast startup cost.

maya: agree. Action items: 1) revert token_budget to 14 in canary (devin), 2) patch kernel selector rule to prefer wide_matmul when queue_depth>1 (sam + li), 3) add kv_lock metrics to console for per-host heatmaps (ashley), 4) monitor canary for 30m then expand.

devin: rolling revert now (canary).

deploy-bot: Deploy triggered by @devin: revert/tokenbudget-canary -> canary. Commit: c4d2e11.

infra-bot: Canary update: token_budget=14 applied. Observe changes in next 3 minutes.

20m later

sam: preliminary: p50_smallreqs back within 5ms of baseline, smallreq_qps recovered ~6%. kv_lock_wait_ms spikes reduced but still slightly above baseline.

li: deploying kernel selector tweak to canary now (no rollout).

deploy-bot: Deploy triggered by @sam: kernel-selector-adjust -> canary. Commit: f0e9d77.

1h later

ashley: metrics look good — p50 and qps mostly recovered. KV lock tail still exists on 2 hosts; I've isolated one host with older CUDA driver and differing stream concurrency. Opening infra ticket to remediate.

maya: thanks all. Summary: regression caused by heuristic change that nudged selector toward mini_fast; mini_fast has higher kernel_start overhead and different KV lock behavior. Short-term fix: revert token_budget and tweak selector rule. Medium-term: harmonize kernel startup paths and add kernel_selector safety thresholds.

devin: I'll file a follow-up PR with automated unit tests that simulate singleton steady-state to avoid future flips.

sam: noted — also adding a flamegraph test in perf harness for kernel_start tail.

maya: great. Closing once infra ticket and PRs are linked. :thumbsup:
